# Media regression fixtures

The tone and video fixtures were generated locally with FFmpeg 9.0.1. They contain only a 440 Hz sine wave or the generated `testsrc2` pattern; there is no third-party recording. Fixture generation may use external tools; application tests and common-codec processing do not.

Audio input: `-f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=0.12 -ac 2`. Outputs: PCM16 WAV, MP3, FLAC, native Vorbis (`-c:a vorbis -strict experimental`), libopus Ogg and WebM, AAC ADTS and M4A, FLAC Matroska. `speech-mode.opus` uses mono `-application voip -b:a 12k`; `surround.opus` duplicates the tone into a 5.1 pan and uses Opus mapping family 1. These protect pure-Rust SILK/voice decoding and standard Opus multistream decoding, without external tools. `ac3.m4a` uses `-c:a ac3` and protects the explicitly approved uncovered-codec fallback.

Video input: `-f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=32x24:rate=10:duration=0.2`. MP4/Matroska use libx264; WebM uses libvpx-vp9. Their track/codec classifications were compared with the original FFprobe backend before removing its process wrappers.

`simple.pdf` is an original two-page 100 × 80 vector document: a red rectangle on page one and a blue rectangle on page two. `compressed.pdf` is an original one-page red rectangle with a zlib-compressed content stream. Both verify a rendered first-page preview and preservation of the original PDF download. Compressed content is expanded under an aggregate byte cap before interpreting its operators.

`photo.heic` is the generated 2048 × 1536 tiled test scene from [heic-rs](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/tree/main/tests/fixtures), encoded by Apple's `sips`; source pixels are generated by its Python script. It is MIT OR Apache-2.0; both license files are included as `photo-LICENSE-*`.

`alpha.heic` and `irot90.heic` are generated colour/gradient fixtures from [imazen/heic at c45113e442c485bb9b4ea37ad53e4d8e82132205](https://github.com/imazen/heic/tree/c45113e442c485bb9b4ea37ad53e4d8e82132205/testdata/features). [Their generator](https://github.com/imazen/heic/blob/c45113e442c485bb9b4ea37ad53e4d8e82132205/scripts/gen_feature_fixtures.py) synthesizes every source pixel and encodes it with libheif/x265; the files contain no third-party artwork or code. These protect 50% auxiliary alpha and a 90° counterclockwise container transform. No code or library from that project is used by RustChan.

`phone-hdr.heic` is an actual iPhone HDR photograph from [John Charankattu's apple-hdr-heic](https://github.com/johncf/apple-hdr-heic), obtained from [the same pinned fixture corpus](https://github.com/imazen/heic/tree/c45113e442c485bb9b4ea37ad53e4d8e82132205/testdata/apple-hdr). Its MIT license is included as `phone-hdr-LICENSE`. The primary SDR picture is decoded; HDR gain-map rendering is outside RustChan's existing thumbnail behaviour.

Final-verification fixtures: `tone-alac.m4a` encodes the generated PCM tone with ALAC; `multiple-streams.mp4` remuxes the generated H.264 video plus AAC and MP3 tracks. `he-aac.m4a` uses the macOS `aac_at` encoder, profile 4, at 48 kbit/s and has backward-compatible SBR signaling (FFprobe reports HE-AAC). `tone.spx` uses the optional Speex 1.2.1 command-line encoder on a 16 kHz mono resampling of the tone. The Speex source was downloaded from the official Xiph distribution and built only in a temporary directory; no Speex application dependency was added. `text.pdf` is an original 100 × 80 document displaying “RustChan” in the standard Helvetica font, with an uncompressed content stream and a flat page tree.

The `opus-surround-distinct.opus` fixture contains six generated sine waves at 233, 331, 449, 71, 557 and 661 Hz, at 48 kHz for 0.24 seconds, encoded with libopus mapping family 1. `opus-surround-padded-gain.opus` adds valid RFC 6716 Appendix B padding to every coded stream and declares +6 dB header gain. `opus-surround-discrete.opus` declares mapping family 255 with a reversed explicit coded-channel map. Each Ogg page checksum and lacing table is regenerated. The matching `-native.f32` files are interleaved little-endian f32 samples decoded by the independent libopus decoder through FFmpeg 9.0.1. They contain 11,520 frames with six channels; production and regression tests do not invoke FFmpeg to read them.

`speex-chained.spx` concatenates two independently numbered copies of the generated tone. `speex-multiplexed.spx` interleaves their corresponding pages, with both BOS headers first. The second logical stream has a distinct serial and recomputed CRCs. These verify per-stream sequence/continuation/EOS validation. Mixed-codec Ogg containers remain outside this validator's classification contract.

`aac-lc-native.f32` is FFmpeg 9.0.1's two-channel, 48 kHz AAC-LC decode of the existing generated `tone.m4a`. Its 5,760 presentation frames exclude the encoder delay and tail padding described by that movie's edit list. The reference protects waveform timing independently of Symphonia's raw packet frame count.

`he-aac-inband.aac` is the same original macOS HE-AAC tone remuxed into ADTS with in-band SBR. Independent decoding yields 12,288 stereo frames at 48 kHz. The patched AAC decoder explicitly reports missing SBR reconstruction; it must never publish the 6,144 core-only frames at 24 kHz as a successful Rust decode.

`inline-image.pdf` is an original 100 × 80 page with one red RGB pixel displayed as a 60 × 60 inline image. It verifies that valid input outside the bounded renderer subset keeps its original download and receives the deterministic SVG preview.

`speex-chained-multiplexed.spx` joins two complete multiplexed groups with four distinct serials and recomputed CRCs. Completed logical streams must not block the next chain’s grouped BOS pages.
